pr.title: Color a collapsed pull request by its row's state, and list its labels in its drawer
pr.head: 62d7c0be84063351b4870d2eecddfb743fb09b5b

summary: Projector's panel is a list in Claude Code, above the prompt, of the pull requests a session fixes or reviews. Each row shows a pull request's number, a state word such as clean or ready, its title, and short notes such as conflict or 2* for two open review threads. When you collapse the list, each pull request shrinks to its number alone, colored to stand in for the word it lost.

Before this change, the collapsed number and the row's word followed two separate rules. The number turned red for a conflict, a change request, or failing checks, and yellow for open threads. The word knew only the review labels and the draft state. So a signed-off pull request that then conflicted showed a red number when collapsed and a green clean when expanded. Nothing on the row said that the checks were failing.
This change makes the state word the single source of color. The word is now the first of these that applies:

WordColorWhen
conflictredThe branch conflicts with its base
failingredThe head's checks fail
changesyellowA review requests changes
threadsyellowReview threads are unresolved
reviewingorangeThe reviewing label is on
cleangreenThe clean label is on
draftdefaultA draft with neither label
readylight blueReady for review, with neither label

A collapsed number takes its word's color, so the two cannot disagree. Because a hold can now hide a clean or reviewing label, the drawer that opens under a row lists every label the pull request carries, drawn in GitHub's own label colors.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One Projector review, at 62d7c0b, requested changes with one open finding: the collapsed-number test never draws a pull request that has both a hold and a review label.
  • All checks passed on this head: the plugin tests, both validates, the type check, the Python suite, project check, and git diff --check.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Hold: something that keeps a pull request from merging or that a review asks for. A conflict, failing checks, a change request, or open threads.
  • Review label: the reviewing or clean label that Projector's review commands set.
  • Watch daemon: the per-machine process that polls GitHub and writes a cache the panel reads.

groups.title: The row's word decides every color
groups.kicker: One ordered list of holds now drives the state word, the notes, and the collapsed number
intro: The new HOLDS list in hooks/register.tsx names the four holds in order of urgency, each with its word, its color, and the note it shows when another hold is the word. rowState takes the first hold that applies, and falls back to the review label, then draft or ready. notesOf leaves out the hold the word already names. statusColor, which colors a collapsed number, is now just the word's color, or muted while the row loads.

Labels are now objects with a name and a color, not lowercased names, so hasLabel compares names without regard to case. A panel snapshot that an earlier release saved with plain-string labels is dropped rather than drawn.

checks.text: No hold can hide behind a green or orange word: rowState checks every hold before it reads a review label, and statusColor reads only rowState. Checked by reading both functions and by the row test, which expects conflict on a conflicting row that carries clean.

files.note: Adds HOLDS, reorders rowState, rebuilds notesOf and statusColor on it, mutes a loading row's number, and draws labels at the end of the drawer's facts line.

checks.text: changes requested is now a yellow note rather than red, which matches its yellow changes word.
labelStyle picks black or white text by GitHub's perceived-lightness formula and its 0.453 threshold, on the raw sRGB channels, as GitHub's stylesheet does.

files.note: Adds the Label type and makes PullRequest.labels a list of it.

groups.title: Both queries read each label's color
groups.kicker: The panel's query and the watch daemon's query ask GitHub for label colors
intro: The panel gets pull requests either from its own GraphQL query or from the watch daemon's cache, so both queries now ask for each label's color. A scalar field adds no GraphQL cost. labelOf keeps a color only when it is six hex digits, and stores it as #rrggbb. A cache written before this change has no colors, so its labels draw on GitHub's light gray until the daemon's next poll. The daemon itself still reads only label names.

files.note: Asks for color and turns each label node into a Label with labelOf.
Adds color to the daemon's query and its comment.

groups.title: Tests of the words, the colors, and the labels
groups.kicker: Panel tests for each word and color, the drawer's labels, and the old snapshot shape
intro: The row test now draws a pull request for every word and checks its color and italic. The collapsed-number test reads each row's word and color, then collapses the list and checks that each number has the same color. A new drawer test checks label fill and text colors, and a snapshot test checks that string labels from an earlier release are dropped.

checks.text: Open review finding: none of the numbers this test draws has both a hold and a review label. A statusColor that let the label win would give a conflicting clean pull request a green collapsed number, and every test would still pass. Adding '#17', the existing "Signed-off change that now conflicts" fixture, closes the gap.

files.note: Expects labels in GitHub's spelling with a normalized color, and a null color for one GitHub could not have sent.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The panel guide describes the new words, notes, collapsed colors, and labels
intro: docs/plugins.md lists the four new words before the review labels, rewrites the notes paragraph, says a loading row's number is muted, describes the drawer's labels, and replaces the collapsed colors list with a single rule: each number takes its row's word's color.
